scenes.tts: What does a nerve signal look like, and what makes it?
scenes.visual: Dark background. The question appears as on-screen text, one line at a time.
scenes.narration: What does a nerve signal look like, and what makes it?

scenes.tts: Here is the membrane potential of a model squid giant axon, over a few milliseconds.
scenes.visual: Axes draw themselves: vertical axis labelled Vm (mV) from −80 to +50, horizontal axis labelled time (ms). A dashed line marks 0 mV.
scenes.narration: Here is the membrane potential of a model squid giant axon, over a few milliseconds.

scenes.tts: The trace starts flat. This is rest, at about minus 65 millivolts.
scenes.caption: The trace starts flat. This is rest, at about −65 mV.
scenes.visual: A flat teal trace draws slowly at −65 mV. Label appears: rest, −65 mV.
scenes.narration: The trace starts flat. This is rest, at about −65 mV.

scenes.tts: Now we nudge it. A small nudge dies away. So does another.
scenes.visual: A small stimulus tick appears under the time axis; the trace bumps up a few millivolts and decays back. A second small bump, same result.
scenes.narration: Now we nudge it. A small nudge dies away. So does another.

scenes.tts: A slightly bigger nudge crosses a line. For this stimulus, that line is threshold. Past it, the voltage keeps rising on its own.
scenes.visual: A dashed amber line labelled threshold (for this stimulus) appears a little above rest. A larger bump reaches it, and the trace keeps climbing.
scenes.narration: A slightly bigger nudge crosses a line. For this stimulus, that line is threshold. Past it, the voltage keeps rising on its own.

scenes.tts: It shoots up in a fraction of a millisecond. This is the rising phase.
scenes.visual: Slow-motion: the steep upstroke draws. Label: rising phase.
scenes.narration: It shoots up in a fraction of a millisecond. This is the rising phase.

scenes.tts: It crosses zero and keeps going. At the peak the inside is positive, about plus 40 millivolts. Going past zero is the overshoot.
scenes.caption: It crosses zero and keeps going. At the peak the inside is positive, about +40 mV. Going past zero is the overshoot.
scenes.visual: The trace crosses the 0 mV dashed line; the part above zero is shaded and labelled overshoot. Label at the top: peak, about +40 mV.
scenes.narration: It crosses zero and keeps going. At the peak the inside is positive, about +40 mV. Going past zero is the overshoot.

scenes.tts: Then the falling phase brings it back down, past rest.
scenes.visual: The downstroke draws and passes −65 mV. Label: falling phase.
scenes.narration: Then the falling phase brings it back down, past rest.

scenes.tts: It dips below rest for several milliseconds. That is the undershoot. Then it settles back.
scenes.visual: The trace sags below the rest line, then creeps back up to −65 mV. Label: undershoot.
scenes.narration: It dips below rest for several milliseconds. That is the undershoot. Then it settles back.

scenes.tts: The whole event is an action potential, or spike. It lasts a few milliseconds.
scenes.visual: All six labels are now visible on the full trace: rest, threshold, rising phase, peak, falling phase, undershoot. Title above: action potential (spike).
scenes.narration: The whole event is an action potential, or spike. It lasts a few milliseconds.

scenes.tts: In 1939 Alan Hodgkin and Andrew Huxley recorded this from inside a squid giant axon. The overshoot was a surprise.
scenes.visual: Simple drawing of a squid giant axon with a fine electrode threaded down its inside. Caption: Hodgkin and Huxley, 1939.
scenes.narration: In 1939 Alan Hodgkin and Andrew Huxley recorded this from inside a squid giant axon. The overshoot was a surprise.

scenes.tts: The leading theory said the voltage should stop near zero. It did not.
scenes.visual: A grey dashed trace that rises and flattens at 0 mV, labelled old theory, sits beside the real trace, which overshoots.
scenes.narration: The leading theory said the voltage should stop near zero. It did not.

scenes.tts: A question to hold. If we push much harder, will the spike be bigger?
scenes.visual: On screen: Pause. A much bigger push: a bigger spike?
scenes.narration: A question to hold. If we push much harder, will the spike be bigger?

scenes.visual: the question stays on screen

scenes.tts: No. It comes sooner, but it is essentially the same size. With brief pushes from rest, the height barely changes. This is all-or-none.
scenes.visual: Three traces overlay: just-threshold, bigger and much bigger brief stimulus. The spikes have roughly equal heights (do not draw them identical); the bigger stimuli fire earlier. Label: all-or-none.
scenes.narration: No. It comes sooner, but it is essentially the same size. With brief pushes from rest, the height barely changes. This is all-or-none.

scenes.tts: Now two pushes close together. The first fires. The second fails. This is refractoriness.
scenes.visual: Two stimulus ticks a short interval apart. The first fires a full spike; after the second, the trace barely moves. Label: refractory.
scenes.narration: Now two pushes close together. The first fires. The second fails. This is refractoriness.

scenes.tts: So we have puzzles. Why the overshoot? Why a threshold? Why all-or-none? Why refractoriness?
scenes.visual: A checklist builds on the right: overshoot, threshold, all-or-none, refractoriness.
scenes.narration: So we have puzzles. Why the overshoot? Why a threshold? Why all-or-none? Why refractoriness?

scenes.tts: And why does the spike travel along the axon without turning back?
scenes.visual: A fifth item joins the checklist: travel. A small axon drawing shows a spike moving left to right.
scenes.narration: And why does the spike travel along the axon without turning back?

scenes.tts: One rule, three gates and a little cable theory answer all five.
scenes.visual: The checklist dims slightly; a teaser of a rope-and-marker voltage scale fades in at the bottom.
scenes.narration: One rule, three gates and a little cable theory answer all five.

scenes.tts: A spike is all or none. It has a threshold. And it needs a rest before the next one.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card on screen: A spike is all or none, has a threshold, and needs a rest before the next one.
scenes.narration: A spike is all or none. It has a threshold. And it needs a rest before the next one.
